skills.title: Compute squares and recognise square numbers
Describe patterns in squares: last digits, odd-number sums, gaps between squares
Decide whether a number can be a perfect square using its last digits and trailing zeros

expectations: A square number is a number times itself, like 7 × 7 = 49, and it can be arranged as a square of dots or tiles
Squaring is not doubling: 5² means 5 × 5 = 25, not 5 + 5 = 10
The sum of the first n odd numbers is n², because each odd number adds an L-shaped layer around the previous square
Squares can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9, so a number ending in 2, 3, 7 or 8 is never a perfect square
A good last digit does not prove a number is a square; the last digit can only rule numbers out
Between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n non-square numbers

misconceptions.belief: Thinks squaring means doubling (5² = 10)
signs: Says 9² is 18
Reads the small 2 as 'times 2'
Lists square numbers as 2, 4, 6, 8

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is 9²?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 9² kitna hota hai?

remediation.representation: A 9 by 9 tile square next to a row of 9 + 9 tiles

misconceptions.belief: Believes a number ending in 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9 (for example ending in 6) must be a perfect square
signs: Calls 26 or 46 a perfect square because it ends in 6
Stops checking once the last digit 'looks right'
Uses the last-digit rule to say yes rather than only no

diagnostic.prompt_en: Mohit says: '146 ends in 6, so it is a perfect square.' Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Mohit bolta hai: '146 ke end mein 6 hai, toh yeh perfect square hai.' Kya woh sahi hai?

options.text: No: 12² = 144 and 13² = 169, so 146 is not a square; ending in 6 only allows it
Yes, every number ending in 6 is a square
Yes, because 6 is an even number

remediation.representation: A list of numbers ending in 6 (16, 26, 36, 46, 56, 66) with the real squares circled
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts which are squares, then checks each against the squares list; ask what the last digit can and cannot tell us

misconceptions.belief: Thinks any number ending in zeros can be a square, ignoring that squares end in an even number of zeros
signs: Says 4000 might be a perfect square
Says 90 is a square because 9 is a square
Ignores counting the trailing zeros

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these could be a perfect square: 4,000 or 40,000?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inmein se kaun perfect square ho sakta hai: 4,000 ya 40,000?

options.text: 40,000, because it ends in an even number of zeros (it is 200²)

remediation.representation: Squares of 2, 20, 200 written one under the other: 4, 400, 40000
remediation.moveShape: Child spots how the zeros grow two at a time; ask what happens to the zeros when a number ending in 0 is multiplied by itself

items.prompt_en: What is 13²?
items.prompt_hi: 13 ka square kitna hai?
hints: What does the small 2 tell you to do?

items.prompt_en: Add the first 8 odd numbers: 1 + 3 + 5 + … + 15. Can you get it without adding one by one?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle 8 odd numbers jodo: 1 + 3 + 5 + … + 15. Ek-ek karke jode bina nikaal sakte ho?
hints: How many odd numbers are we adding?
The first n odd numbers always add up to a square.

items.prompt_en: Before you multiply, predict the last digit of 47².
items.prompt_hi: Multiply karne se pehle guess karo: 47² ka last digit kya hoga?
hints: Which digit decides the last digit of a product?

items.prompt_en: Can 2,738 be a perfect square? Tell me how you know without finding any square root.
items.prompt_hi: Kya 2,738 perfect square ho sakta hai? Square root nikale bina batao kaise pata chala.
items.answer: No, because no square ends in 8; squares only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9
hints: Look at the last digit. What is it?
Think of the last digits of 1², 2², … 9².
Squares end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9; is 8 on that list?
No: a square can never end in 8, so 2,738 is not a square.

items.prompt_en: 26 and 36 both end in 6. Which one is a perfect square, and what does that tell you about the 'ends in 6' clue?
items.prompt_hi: 26 aur 36 dono 6 pe khatam hote hain. Inmein se perfect square kaun hai, aur isse '6 pe khatam' wale clue ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
items.answer: 36 is a square (6²) but 26 is not, so ending in 6 does not prove a number is a square
hints: Check each against the squares you know.
26 sits between 5² and 6², so it is ___ a square.
Only 36 is a square: the last digit can rule out, not prove.

items.prompt_en: Riya wrote: 15² = 30 and 20² = 40. Check her work and fix it.
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne likha: 15² = 30 aur 20² = 40. Uska kaam check karo aur theek karo.
items.answer: She doubled instead of squaring: 15² = 225 and 20² = 400
hints: What does she seem to be doing to each number?
She multiplied by 2; squaring multiplies the number by itself.

items.prompt_en: For PT drill, 50 students must stand in a full square formation. What is the biggest square possible, and how many students are left out?
items.prompt_hi: PT drill mein 50 bachchon ko poore square mein khada karna hai. Sabse bada square kitna banega, aur kitne bachche bach jaayenge?
items.answer: 7 rows of 7 = 49 students, so 1 student is left out
hints: Which square numbers are close to 50?
64 is too many, so use ___ and 50 − 49 = ___.

items.prompt_en: A 5 by 5 square of dots grows into a 6 by 6 square. How many dots are added, and which odd number is that?
items.prompt_hi: 5 by 5 dots ka square badhkar 6 by 6 ban jaata hai. Kitne dots jude, aur woh kaunsa odd number hai?
items.answer: 11 dots are added, the 6th odd number (36 − 25 = 11)
hints: Picture the new row and the new column.
New row of 6 and new column of 6 share one corner dot.
11 dots: the L-shaped layer, the 6th odd number.

items.prompt_en: A school wants a square courtyard of tiles using all of 1,000 tiles. Is that possible? If not, what is the fewest extra tiles needed to make a full square?
items.prompt_hi: School ek square courtyard banana chahta hai, poore 1,000 tiles se. Kya yeh ho sakta hai? Agar nahi, toh kam se kam kitne tiles aur chahiye poora square banane ke liye?
items.answer: Not possible; 31² = 961 and 32² = 1024, so 24 more tiles make a 32 by 32 square
hints: Odd number of zeros at the end: can 1,000 be a square?
Find the squares just below and just above 1,000.

items.prompt_en: How many non-square numbers lie between 12² and 13²?
items.prompt_hi: 12² aur 13² ke beech kitne aise numbers hain jo square nahi hain?
hints: 144 and 169; count the numbers strictly between them.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger cousin why 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 always gives a square number. Use a picture in your explanation.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 hamesha square number kyun deta hai. Ek picture se samjhao.
items.answer: Each odd number is an L-shaped layer that wraps around the previous square, making the next bigger square; 4 layers make a 4 by 4 square = 16
hints: Start with 1 dot. What does adding 3 dots make?
Adding 3 dots in an L turns 1 dot into a 2 by 2 square.
Each next odd number wraps an L around the square; after 1, 3, 5, 7 the square is ___ by ___.
Odd numbers are L-layers; four of them build a 4 by 4 square of 16.

items.prompt_en: Without full calculation, which of these could be perfect squares: 1,089; 4,322; 7,057; 5,625?
items.prompt_hi: Poora calculate kiye bina batao, inmein se kaun perfect square ho sakte hain: 1,089; 4,322; 7,057; 5,625?
items.answer: Only 1,089 and 5,625 can be (they are 33² and 75²); 4,322 ends in 2 and 7,057 ends in 7
hints: What is the quick first check?
Look at last digits: which endings are impossible for squares?
2 and 7 are impossible endings, so ___ and ___ are out.
1,089 (33²) and 5,625 (75²) are squares; the other two cannot be.

skills.title: Find square roots of perfect squares by prime factorisation
Estimate square roots of non-square numbers between consecutive integers
Reason about square roots: last digit of roots and why √(a + b) ≠ √a + √b

expectations: The square root of n is the number which, multiplied by itself, gives n; it is the side of a square with area n
To find a square root by prime factorisation, pair up equal prime factors and take one from each pair
If some prime factor is left without a pair, the number is not a perfect square
A non-square number has a square root between two consecutive whole numbers, found from the squares on either side
Square root is not halving: √64 = 8, not 32

misconceptions.belief: Thinks √(a + b) = √a + √b
signs: Splits the root across a plus sign
Is surprised that the side of a combined area is not the sum of sides

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is √(9 + 16)?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: √(9 + 16) kitna hai?

remediation.representation: A 3 by 3 square and a 4 by 4 square of tiles rearranged into one 5 by 5 square
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the side of the combined square, then counts 25 tiles; ask why the side is 5 and not 3 + 4

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the square root is half the number
signs: Says √64 = 32
Confuses 'root' with dividing by 2

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is √100?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: √100 kitna hai?

remediation.representation: A 10 by 10 grid of 100 squares with its side marked
remediation.moveShape: Child checks the claimed root by multiplying it by itself; ask whether 50 × 50 gives 100

misconceptions.belief: In prime factorisation, multiplies all the primes (or both from each pair) instead of one from each pair
signs: Gets √144 = 144 or 72 from the factor list
Takes 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 from 2⁴ × 3² and gets 36
Cannot say what 'pairing' is for

remediation.representation: Prime factors shown as matched pairs of coloured beads, one bead from each pair moved to a 'root' tray
remediation.moveShape: Child groups the factors into two identical halves and checks that one half times itself is the number

items.prompt_en: Find √324 using prime factorisation.
items.prompt_hi: Prime factorisation se √324 nikaalo.

items.prompt_en: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does √70 lie?
items.prompt_hi: √70 kin do lagatar whole numbers ke beech aata hai?
items.answer: Between 8 and 9

items.prompt_en: Predict first, then check: is √(9 + 16) the same as √9 + √16?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo, phir check karo: kya √(9 + 16) aur √9 + √16 same hain?
hints: Not equal: 5 versus 7. A root does not split across a plus sign.

items.prompt_en: A square plot of land has an area of 576 m². How long is each side?
items.prompt_hi: Ek square plot ka area 576 m² hai. Har side kitni lambi hai?
hints: Side × side = area. Which number times itself gives 576?

items.prompt_en: Neha wrote: √(36 + 64) = 6 + 8 = 14. Find her mistake and the correct answer.
items.prompt_hi: Neha ne likha: √(36 + 64) = 6 + 8 = 14. Galti dhoondho aur sahi answer batao.
items.answer: She split the root over the plus sign; 36 + 64 = 100 and √100 = 10
hints: Do the bracket first. What is 36 + 64?
The root acts on the whole 100.

items.prompt_en: Why must √2000 be between 44 and 45?
items.prompt_hi: √2000 44 aur 45 ke beech hi kyun hona chahiye?
items.answer: Because 44² = 1936 is less than 2000 and 45² = 2025 is more than 2000

items.prompt_en: One of 1,296 and 1,250 is a perfect square. Use prime factors to decide which.
items.prompt_hi: 1,296 aur 1,250 mein se ek perfect square hai. Prime factors se decide karo kaunsa.
items.answer: 1,296 = 2⁴ × 3⁴ is a square (36²); 1,250 = 2 × 5⁴ has an unpaired 2, so it is not
hints: Which one has a prime left without a partner?
1,296 is 36²; 1,250 has a lonely 2, so it is not a square.

items.prompt_en: 49 square tiles are arranged into one big square. How many tiles long is each side, and how is that the square root?
items.prompt_hi: 49 square tiles se ek bada square banaya. Har side kitne tiles lambi hai, aur yeh square root kaise hai?
items.answer: 7 tiles; the side of a square of area 49 is √49 = 7
hints: Each side is 7 tiles: the side is the square root of the area.

items.prompt_en: A square kitchen garden must have area 200 m². Estimate its side to one decimal place.
items.prompt_hi: Ek square kitchen garden ka area 200 m² hona chahiye. Uski side ek decimal tak estimate karo.
hints: 14² = 196 and 15² = 225, so the side is a bit more than 14.
Try 14.1² = 198.81 and 14.2² = 201.64; which is closer to 200?

items.prompt_en: What is the smallest number you must multiply 180 by to get a perfect square? What is the square root of the result?
items.prompt_hi: 180 ko kam se kam kis number se multiply karein ki perfect square ban jaaye? Result ka square root kya hoga?
hints: Which prime has no partner? Multiply by ___.
Multiply by 5 to get 900, whose root is 30.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how pairing prime factors gives you the square root, using 144 as your example.
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki prime factors ki pairing se square root kaise milta hai, 144 ka example lekar.
items.answer: 144 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; split into two identical groups (2 × 2 × 3)(2 × 2 × 3); one group = 12 is the root because 12 × 12 = 144
hints: Write 144 as a product of primes.
Make two identical groups; each group equals ___.

items.prompt_en: Without working it out fully, what could the last digit of √7,744 be?
items.prompt_hi: Poora nikale bina batao, √7,744 ka last digit kya ho sakta hai?
items.answer: 2 or 8 (it is 88)
hints: Which digits, when squared, end in 4?
So the root ends in ___ or ___.
The root ends in 2 or 8; in fact √7,744 = 88.

skills.title: Compute cubes and recognise perfect cubes
Find cube roots by prime factorisation using triplets
Explore sums of cubes and taxicab numbers like 1729

expectations: A cube number is a number used three times in a multiplication: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, the number of small cubes in a 4 by 4 by 4 block
Cubing is not multiplying by 3: 4³ is 64, not 12
For a cube root, group equal prime factors in threes and take one from each triplet
If any prime factor cannot be grouped into a triplet, the number is not a perfect cube
Doubling the edge of a cube makes its volume 8 times bigger, since 2³ = 8
1729 is the smallest number that is a sum of two cubes in two different ways: 1³ + 12³ and 9³ + 10³

misconceptions.belief: Confuses cubing with multiplying by 3
signs: Says 4³ = 12
Says 10³ = 30
Reads the small 3 as 'times 3'

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is 5³?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 5³ kitna hota hai?

remediation.moveShape: Child counts one layer, then the layers; ask how 'three fives multiplied' differs from 'three fives added'

misconceptions.belief: Mixes up cubes and squares, multiplying the number only twice
signs: Says 5³ = 25
Uses pairs instead of triplets when finding cube roots
Says 64 has cube root 8

diagnostic.prompt_en: 8,000 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5. What is its cube root?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 8,000 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5. Iska cube root kya hai?

remediation.representation: Prime factors grouped as coloured triplets, with one from each triplet moved to the 'root' tray
remediation.moveShape: Child regroups pairs into triplets and multiplies one from each; then cubes the result to check

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the cube root means dividing by 3
signs: Says ∛27 = 9

items.prompt_hi: Kabir ne likha: 4³ = 12 aur 10³ = 30. Kya galat hua? Sahi answers batao.
items.answer: He multiplied by 3 instead of cubing: 4³ = 64 and 10³ = 1000
hints: What did Kabir do to 4 to get 12?
Cubing means using the number three times in a multiplication.

items.prompt_en: Find ∛2,744 using prime factorisation.
items.prompt_hi: Prime factorisation se ∛2,744 nikaalo.
hints: Divide 2,744 by 2 as many times as you can.

items.prompt_en: A cube is built from small unit cubes. If you double the length of its edge, predict how many times as many unit cubes you need.
items.prompt_hi: Ek cube chhote unit cubes se bana hai. Agar edge ki length double kar do, toh guess karo kitne guna zyada unit cubes lagenge?
items.answer: 8 times, because 2³ = 8
hints: Try it with an edge of 1, then 2.
Doubling multiplies each of three dimensions by 2: 2 × 2 × 2 = ___

items.prompt_en: Ludo dice are stacked into a big solid cube with 5 dice along each edge. How many dice are used?
items.prompt_hi: Ludo ke dice ek bade solid cube mein lagaye hain, har edge pe 5 dice. Kitne dice lage?
hints: How many dice in one layer?

items.prompt_en: Is 500 a perfect cube? Explain using its prime factors, and say the smallest number to multiply it by to make one.
items.prompt_hi: Kya 500 perfect cube hai? Prime factors se samjhao, aur batao kis sabse chhote number se multiply karein toh perfect cube ban jaaye.
items.answer: No: 500 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5; the two 2s are not a triplet. Multiply by 2 to get 1,000 = 10³
hints: The 5s make a triplet; the 2s need one more 2. Multiply by ___.
Not a cube; multiplying by 2 gives 1,000 = 10³.

items.prompt_en: Look at 36, 27 and 64. Which is a square only, which is a cube only, and which is both?
items.prompt_hi: 36, 27 aur 64 ko dekho. Kaun sirf square hai, kaun sirf cube, aur kaun dono?
items.answer: 36 is a square only (6²), 27 is a cube only (3³), 64 is both (8² and 4³)
hints: Write each as n × n if you can.
Now try each as n × n × n.

items.prompt_en: Ramanujan said 1729 is special. Show that 1729 can be written as a sum of two cubes in two different ways.
items.prompt_hi: Ramanujan ne kaha tha 1729 khaas hai. Dikhao ki 1729 ko do alag tareekon se do cubes ke sum mein likh sakte hain.
acceptable: 1 cubed plus 12 cubed and 9 cubed plus 10 cubed

items.prompt_en: Describe 3³ as a stack of blocks: how many blocks in a layer, how many layers, how many in total?
items.prompt_hi: 3³ ko blocks ke stack ki tarah batao: ek layer mein kitne blocks, kitni layers, total kitne?
items.answer: 9 blocks in a 3 by 3 layer, 3 layers, 27 blocks in total
hints: A layer is a square of blocks. How big?

items.prompt_en: What is ∛3,375? Hint: think about the last digit first.
items.prompt_hi: ∛3,375 kya hai? Hint: pehle last digit ke baare mein socho.
hints: A cube ending in 5 comes from a number ending in ___.
So the root is between 10 and 20 and ends in 5: ___

items.prompt_en: Explain to a classmate the one difference between finding a square root and a cube root by prime factorisation.
items.prompt_hi: Ek classmate ko samjhao: prime factorisation se square root aur cube root nikaalne mein ek main fark kya hai?
items.answer: For a square root group equal primes in pairs; for a cube root group them in triplets, then take one from each group
acceptable: pairs for square root, threes for cube root
hints: How do we group primes for a square root?
For a cube root, three equal factors must go together.
Square root: groups of ___; cube root: groups of ___.
Pairs for square roots, triplets for cube roots, one from each group.

items.prompt_en: Without multiplying it all out, what is the last digit of 27³?
items.prompt_hi: Poora multiply kiye bina batao, 27³ ka last digit kya hoga?

skills.title: Write repeated multiplication in exponential form and name base and exponent
Evaluate powers, including powers of negative numbers
Compare how fast powers grow against repeated addition

expectations: aⁿ means a multiplied by itself n times; a is the base and n is the exponent
The base and exponent cannot be swapped: 2⁵ = 32 but 5² = 25
Powers grow much faster than repeated addition: doubling 10 times gives 1,024
A negative base raised to an even power is positive and to an odd power is negative
Powers of 10 match the place values: 10⁵ = 1,00,000 (one lakh)

misconceptions.belief: Reads 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6
signs: Says 3⁴ = 12
Says 10³ = 30
Treats the exponent as a multiplier

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3⁴ kitna hai?

remediation.moveShape: Child counts the branches at each level (3, 9, 27, 81); ask what 'four times' means in this picture

items.answer: 5⁴; base 5, exponent 4

items.prompt_en: What is 2⁵?

items.prompt_en: A sheet of paper is folded in half 10 times. Before working it out, predict: more or fewer than 100 layers?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kaagaz ko 10 baar aadha fold karte hain. Calculate karne se pehle guess karo: 100 layers se zyada ya kam?
items.answer: More: 2¹⁰ = 1,024 layers
hints: Each fold does what to the number of layers?

items.prompt_en: Which is bigger: 2⁵ or 5²? By how much?
items.prompt_hi: Kaun bada hai: 2⁵ ya 5²? Kitna zyada?
items.answer: 2⁵ = 32 is bigger than 5² = 25, by 7

items.prompt_en: A message is forwarded on a phone chain. In round 1, one person sends it to 3 people. In each next round, everyone who just got it sends it to 3 new people. How many people get it in round 4?
items.prompt_hi: Ek message phone chain mein forward hota hai. Round 1 mein ek insaan 3 logon ko bhejta hai. Har agle round mein jisne abhi paaya woh 3 naye logon ko bhejta hai. Round 4 mein kitne log message paayenge?
hints: How many receive it in round 1 and round 2?
Round 1: 3, round 2: 9; each round multiplies by 3.

items.prompt_en: Why does doubling a number 20 times give a much bigger result than adding 1,000 twenty times?
items.prompt_hi: Ek number ko 20 baar double karna, 1,000 ko 20 baar jodne se bahut bada result kyun deta hai?
items.answer: Doubling multiplies the whole amount each time, so it grows faster and faster: 2²⁰ = 1,048,576 (over 10 lakh) while adding 1,000 twenty times gives only 20,000
hints: What does each step add when you add 1,000?
Adding always adds the same 1,000; doubling adds the whole current amount.
Doubling: over 10 lakh; adding: 20,000. Multiplying snowballs.

items.prompt_en: Write 10⁶ as an ordinary number and say it in the Indian number system.
items.prompt_hi: 10⁶ ko ordinary number mein likho aur Indian number system mein bolo.
items.answer: 10,00,000, which is ten lakh
hints: 1,00,000 is one lakh, so 10,00,000 is ___ lakh.

items.prompt_en: Offer A: ₹1 on day 1, ₹2 on day 2, ₹4 on day 3, doubling every day. Offer B: ₹10 lakh in one go. On day 30 alone, how much does Offer A give?
items.prompt_hi: Offer A: day 1 ko ₹1, day 2 ko ₹2, day 3 ko ₹4, har din double. Offer B: ek baar mein ₹10 lakh. Sirf day 30 ko Offer A kitna dega?
items.answer: 2²⁹ = ₹53,68,70,912 (over ₹53 crore), far more than ₹10 lakh
hints: What power of 2 is paid on day 1, day 2, day 3?

items.prompt_en: Find (−2)⁴ and (−2)³. Why is one positive and one negative?

items.prompt_en: A tree trunk splits into 2 branches, and every new branch splits into 2 again. After 5 rounds of splitting, how many newest branches are there?
items.prompt_hi: Ek ped ka tana 2 shaakhaon mein batta hai, aur har nayi shaakha phir 2 mein batti hai. 5 baar batne ke baad sabse nayi kitni shaakhaen hongi?

items.prompt_en: In the Koch curve, each straight segment is replaced by 4 segments, each 1/3 as long. Starting with one 9 cm segment, how many segments and what total length after 2 stages?
items.prompt_hi: Koch curve mein har seedha tukda 4 tukdon se badal jaata hai, har ek 1/3 lamba. Ek 9 cm ke tukde se shuru karke, 2 stages ke baad kitne tukde aur kul length kitni?
items.answer: 16 segments of 1 cm each: total 16 cm
hints: After stage 1: how many segments and how long?
16 segments, 16 cm; the length grows by 4/3 each stage.

items.prompt_en: A rangoli shows Sierpinski stage 2 drawn on a grid of 16 tiny triangles. How many tiny triangles are coloured, and what fraction of the big triangle is that?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rangoli mein 16 chhote triangles ke grid pe Sierpinski stage 2 bani hai. Kitne chhote triangles rangeen hain, aur yeh bade triangle ka kitna hissa hai?
hints: How many shaded triangles does stage 2 have?

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend what makes a shape a fractal, using the Sierpinski triangle.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko Sierpinski triangle se samjhao ki koi shape fractal kab hota hai.
items.answer: The same rule is repeated on every piece at smaller and smaller sizes, so each part looks like a smaller copy of the whole
hints: What do we do at every stage?
Apply the same rule to every shaded piece.
So any small part looks like ___
A repeated rule making self-similar smaller copies.

items.prompt_en: What fraction of the big triangle is still shaded after stage 1 of the Sierpinski triangle?
items.prompt_hi: Sierpinski triangle ki stage 1 ke baad bade triangle ka kitna hissa shaded rehta hai?
hints: Into how many equal triangles is it split?
4, and the middle one is removed.

items.prompt_en: At stage 3 of the Sierpinski triangle, how many shaded triangles are there, and what fraction of the area is shaded?
items.prompt_hi: Sierpinski triangle ki stage 3 pe kitne shaded triangles hain, aur area ka kitna hissa shaded hai?
items.answer: 27 triangles; (3/4)³ = 27/64 of the area

workedExample.problem: Count the shaded triangles and the shaded fraction at stage 2 of the Sierpinski triangle.
steps: Stage 1: each shaded triangle becomes 3; 3 triangles, 3/4 shaded.
Stage 2: each of the 3 becomes 3; 9 triangles.
fadedVersion: Stage 1: each shaded triangle becomes ___; 3 triangles, 3/4 shaded.
Stage 2: each of the 3 becomes 3; ___ triangles.

skills.title: Recognise which arrangements of faces fold into a solid (nets)
Draw and read front, top and side views of solids made of cubes
Count faces, vertices and edges and verify Euler's formula F + V − E = 2

expectations: A net is a flat shape that folds up into a solid; a cube has 11 different nets, but not every arrangement of six squares works
Views from the front, top and side show different shapes of the same solid
For polyhedra (solids with flat faces), F + V − E = 2
Each edge is shared by exactly two faces, so counting edges face by face counts each edge twice
Euler's formula can show that some combinations of faces, vertices and edges are impossible

misconceptions.belief: Believes any arrangement of six squares folds into a cube
signs: Says a row of 6 squares makes a cube
Says a 2 by 3 rectangle of squares is a cube net
Doesn't imagine the folding

diagnostic.prompt_en: Six squares are joined in a 2 by 3 rectangle. Does it fold into a cube?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Chhe squares 2 by 3 rectangle mein jude hain. Kya yeh fold hokar cube banega?

options.text: No; some faces would overlap and others would be missing
Yes, any six squares make a cube
Yes, because a cube has six faces

remediation.representation: An on-screen fold animation of the 2 by 3 net, showing two squares landing on the same face
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts which squares meet, then watches the fold; ask which face of the cube is left open

misconceptions.belief: Counts edges face by face without noticing each edge is shared by two faces
signs: Says a cube has 24 edges
Gets F + V − E as a negative number
Counts the same edge twice

diagnostic.prompt_en: How many edges does a cube have?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Cube ke kitne edges hote hain?

remediation.representation: A cube made of straws and clay, with each straw counted once
remediation.moveShape: Child counts the straws; ask how many faces meet along each straw

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the front, top and side views of a solid look the same
signs: Draws the same picture for all three views
Ignores cubes hidden behind others
Mixes up the top view with the front view

diagnostic.prompt_en: Three cubes are in a row on a table, with one more cube on top of the left one. What is the top view?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Teen cubes mez pe ek line mein hain, aur ek cube left wale ke upar. Top view kaisa dikhega?

remediation.representation: A real stack of 4 cubes photographed from the front, the top and the side
remediation.moveShape: Child matches each photo to a view; ask why the top view shows only 3 squares

items.prompt_en: Count the faces, vertices and edges of a cube, then work out F + V − E.
items.prompt_hi: Cube ke faces, vertices aur edges gino, phir F + V − E nikaalo.
hints: How many faces does a dice have?
Edges: 4 on top, 4 on bottom, 4 upright = ___

items.prompt_en: A triangular prism (like a Toblerone box) has how many faces, vertices and edges? Check Euler's formula.
items.prompt_hi: Triangular prism (jaise Toblerone ka dabba) ke kitne faces, vertices aur edges hain? Euler ka formula check karo.
hints: Count the triangle ends and the rectangle sides.

items.prompt_en: A square pyramid has how many faces, vertices and edges? Check F + V − E.
items.prompt_hi: Square pyramid ke kitne faces, vertices aur edges hain? F + V − E check karo.
hints: Count the base and the sloping faces.
1 square + 4 triangles = 5 faces; 4 base corners + 1 tip = 5 vertices.
Edges: 4 round the base + 4 up to the tip = ___

items.prompt_en: Six squares are joined in one straight row. Predict: will it fold into a cube?
items.prompt_hi: Chhe squares ek seedhi line mein jude hain. Guess karo: kya yeh cube mein fold hoga?
items.answer: No; four of them wrap around, but the last two overlap, leaving the top and bottom open
hints: Fold the first four into a loop. What's left?
The loop covers 4 sides; the top and bottom are open.
They land on top of the loop, so no top or bottom: not a cube.

items.prompt_en: Aman says: 'Any six squares joined edge to edge make a net of a cube.' Give an example that proves him wrong.
items.prompt_hi: Aman kehta hai: 'Koi bhi chhe squares edge se edge jude hon toh cube ka net bante hain.' Ek example do jo use galat saabit kare.
items.answer: A 2 by 3 rectangle of squares (or a row of 6) does not fold into a cube
hints: Try folding a 2 by 3 block in your mind.
Some faces end up on top of each other.
So at least one face of the cube is ___
The 2 by 3 rectangle is six squares but not a cube net.

items.prompt_en: Compare a cross shape (one square on top, four in a row, one below) with a 2 by 3 block of squares. Which is a cube net?
items.prompt_hi: Cross shape (upar ek square, beech mein chaar ki line, neeche ek) ko 2 by 3 squares ke block se compare karo. Kaunsa cube ka net hai?
items.answer: The cross folds into a cube; the 2 by 3 block doesn't
hints: Fold the row of four in the cross into a loop.
The square above and below become the top and bottom.
In the 2 by 3 block, do you get a top and a bottom?
The cross is a net; the block is not.

items.prompt_en: Can a polyhedron have 7 faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges? Use Euler's formula.
items.prompt_hi: Kya kisi polyhedron ke 7 faces, 8 vertices aur 12 edges ho sakte hain? Euler ka formula use karo.
items.answer: No: 7 + 8 − 12 = 3, but F + V − E must be 2

items.prompt_en: Sahil counted the edges of a cube as 6 faces × 4 edges = 24. What did he miss?
items.prompt_hi: Sahil ne cube ke edges 6 faces × 4 edges = 24 gine. Usse kya chhoot gaya?
items.answer: Each edge is shared by two faces, so he counted each edge twice: 24 ÷ 2 = 12
hints: How many faces meet along each edge?

items.prompt_en: Three cubes sit in a row on a table, with a fourth cube on top of the left one. Describe the front view, the top view and the side view from the right.
items.prompt_hi: Teen cubes mez pe ek line mein hain, aur chautha cube left wale ke upar. Front view, top view aur right side view batao.
items.answer: Front: an L of 4 squares (3 along the bottom, 1 on top at the left); top: a row of 3 squares; right side: 2 squares stacked
hints: From the front, what do you see on the bottom row and on top?
3 along the bottom, 1 above the left.
From above, the top cube hides the cube under it, so you see ___ squares.
Front: L of 4; top: row of 3; side: 2 stacked.

items.prompt_en: You open a sweet box (a cuboid) and flatten it. How many rectangles does its net have, and how many pairs of matching rectangles?
items.prompt_hi: Tum mithai ka dabba (cuboid) khol ke flat karte ho. Uske net mein kitne rectangles hain, aur matching rectangles ki kitni jodiyaan?
items.answer: 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs
hints: How many faces does a box have?
Top, bottom, front, back, left, right.
Opposite faces match, so there are ___ pairs.

items.prompt_en: A football is made of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons. Find its number of edges and vertices.
items.prompt_hi: Ek football 12 pentagons aur 20 hexagons se bana hai. Uske edges aur vertices nikaalo.
hints: Edges: count sides of all faces, then halve: (60 + 120) ÷ 2 = ___

items.prompt_en: Explain Euler's formula to a friend using a cube, and say what kind of solid it works for.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko cube se Euler ka formula samjhao, aur batao yeh kis tarah ke solid pe kaam karta hai.
items.answer: For polyhedra (flat faces, straight edges), faces + vertices − edges = 2; a cube has 6 + 8 − 12 = 2
hints: Count a cube's faces, vertices and edges.
It is always 2 for polyhedra like a cube or pyramid.

items.prompt_en: What is F + V − E for a polyhedron such as a cube or a pyramid?
items.prompt_hi: Cube ya pyramid jaise polyhedron ke liye F + V − E kitna hota hai?

workedExample.problem: Check Euler's formula for a hexagonal prism.
steps: Vertices: 6 on the top hexagon + 6 on the bottom = 12.
Edges: 6 on top + 6 on bottom + 6 upright = 18.
fadedVersion: Vertices: 6 on the top hexagon + 6 on the bottom = ___.
Edges: 6 on top + 6 on bottom + 6 upright = ___.

skills.title: Compute the mean of a data set
Interpret the mean as a balance point and a levelling of values
Use the mean to find missing values and predict how it changes

expectations: Mean = sum of the values ÷ number of values
The mean is the level you'd get if all values were evened out; the amounts above it exactly balance the amounts below it
The mean is not the same as the middle value, and it doesn't have to be one of the data values
One very large or small value (an outlier) can pull the mean a lot
If you know the mean and the count, you know the total: total = mean × count

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the mean is the middle value in the list
signs: Picks the middle number as the 'average'
Doesn't add up the values
Gives the same answer for mean and median

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is the mean of 3, 9, 4, 10, 4?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3, 9, 4, 10, 4 ka mean kya hai?

remediation.representation: Towers of blocks of heights 3, 9, 4, 10, 4, then levelled by moving blocks
remediation.moveShape: Child moves blocks from tall towers to short ones until all are equal; ask how tall each tower ends up

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the mean must be one of the data values
signs: Rejects 3 as the mean of 1, 2, 4, 5 because 3 isn't in the list
Rounds the mean to the nearest data value
Says 'average family has 2.5 children' is impossible so the maths is wrong

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is the mean of 1, 2, 4, 5?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 1, 2, 4, 5 ka mean kya hai?

options.text: 3, even though 3 isn't in the list
There is no mean because no value is in the middle

remediation.representation: A see-saw number line with weights at 1, 2, 4 and 5, balancing on a pivot at 3
remediation.moveShape: Child slides the pivot until it balances; ask whether the pivot needs to be under a weight

misconceptions.belief: Thinks one unusual value doesn't change the mean much
signs: Says the mean of 2, 2, 2, 50 is about 2
Uses the mean to describe 'typical' data with an outlier
Is surprised the mean moves a lot

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is the mean of 2, 2, 2 and 50?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 2, 2, 2 aur 50 ka mean kya hai?

remediation.representation: A balance beam with three weights at 2 and one far away at 50
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts where the beam balances, then calculates; ask how far the single weight pulled the pivot

items.prompt_en: Find the mean of 6, 8, 7, 9 and 5.
items.prompt_hi: 6, 8, 7, 9 aur 5 ka mean nikaalo.

items.prompt_en: Find the mean of 12, 15, 18, 21 and 9.
items.prompt_hi: 12, 15, 18, 21 aur 9 ka mean nikaalo.

items.prompt_en: Arjun said the mean of 3, 9, 4, 10, 4 is 4 because it's the middle number after sorting. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Arjun ne kaha 3, 9, 4, 10, 4 ka mean 4 hai kyunki sort karne ke baad beech mein yahi hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No; that's the middle value. Mean = (3 + 9 + 4 + 10 + 4) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6
hints: What two steps make a mean?
Add everything, then divide by how many.

items.prompt_en: The mean of 4, 6 and 8 is 6. Predict: if you add another 6 to the list, does the mean go up, go down or stay the same?
items.prompt_hi: 4, 6 aur 8 ka mean 6 hai. Guess karo: agar list mein ek aur 6 jod do, toh mean badhega, ghatega ya same rahega?
hints: Is the new value above, below or at the mean?
It sits exactly at the balance point.

items.prompt_en: The mean of 2, 5 and 11 is 6. Show that the distances below the mean balance the distances above it.
items.prompt_hi: 2, 5 aur 11 ka mean 6 hai. Dikhao ki mean se neeche ki dooriyan upar ki doori ko balance karti hain.
items.answer: 2 is 4 below and 5 is 1 below (5 in total); 11 is 5 above, so they balance exactly
hints: How far is each value from 6?

items.prompt_en: The mean of four numbers is 15. Three of them are 12, 18 and 10. Find the fourth.
items.prompt_hi: Chaar numbers ka mean 15 hai. Unmein se teen 12, 18 aur 10 hain. Chautha nikaalo.
hints: What must the total of the four numbers be?

items.prompt_en: For the data 2, 2, 2, 50, find the mean and the middle value. Which describes most of the data better?
items.prompt_hi: Data 2, 2, 2, 50 ke liye mean aur middle value nikaalo. Zyaadatar data ko kaun behtar batata hai?
items.answer: Mean 14, middle value 2; the middle value describes most of the data better because one big value pulls the mean up
hints: Add and divide for the mean.
Mean = ___; the middle value of 2, 2, 2, 50 is 2.
Mean 14 is pulled up by 50; 2 is more typical.

items.prompt_en: The noon temperatures in a week were 28, 30, 31, 29, 32, 30 and 30 °C. Find the mean temperature.
items.prompt_hi: Ek hafte mein dopahar ka taapmaan 28, 30, 31, 29, 32, 30 aur 30 °C tha. Mean taapmaan nikaalo.

items.prompt_en: A batter has an average of 40 runs over 9 innings. How many must she score in the 10th innings to raise her average to 42?
items.prompt_hi: Ek batter ka 9 innings mein average 40 runs hai. 10th innings mein kitne run banaye ki average 42 ho jaaye?
items.answer: 60 runs
hints: What is her total so far?
For an average of 42 over 10 innings she needs 420; 420 − 360 = ___

items.prompt_en: Three towers have 3, 7 and 5 blocks. Move blocks so all towers are the same height. How tall is each, and what does that number mean?
items.prompt_hi: Teen towers mein 3, 7 aur 5 blocks hain. Blocks hilaa ke sabko barabar oonchai ka karo. Har ek kitna ooncha hai, aur yeh number kya hai?
items.answer: 5 blocks each; that is the mean
hints: How many blocks are there in all?

items.prompt_en: Isha says the mean of 1, 2, 4, 5 can't be 3 because 3 isn't one of the numbers. Is she right?
items.prompt_hi: Isha kehti hai 1, 2, 4, 5 ka mean 3 nahi ho sakta kyunki 3 inmein se koi number nahi hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No; the mean is 12 ÷ 4 = 3, and the mean doesn't have to be a data value
hints: = ___; is that allowed to be outside the list?

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger student what the mean tells you, using towers of blocks or sharing sweets.
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote student ko blocks ke towers ya mithai baant ke samjhao ki mean kya batata hai.
items.answer: The mean is how many each would have if everything were shared out equally: add all the amounts and divide by how many there are
hints: If 3 friends have 2, 4 and 6 sweets and pool them, how many are there?

items.prompt_en: Find the mean of 10, 20, 30 and 40.
items.prompt_hi: 10, 20, 30 aur 40 ka mean nikaalo.

workedExample.problem: Five friends have ₹40, ₹55, ₹30, ₹65 and ₹60. Find the mean amount and check the balance.
steps: Below 50: 40 is 10 less, 30 is 20 less, total 30 below.
Above 50: 55 is 5 more, 65 is 15 more, 60 is 10 more, total 30 above.
30 below balances 30 above, so ₹50 is correct.
fadedVersion: Below 50: 40 is 10 less, 30 is 20 less, total ___ below.
Above 50: 55 is 5 more, 65 is 15 more, 60 is 10 more, total ___ above.

skills.title: Read values and describe trends from a line graph
Draw a line graph with sensible axes and scale
Decide when a line graph is appropriate and estimate between points

expectations: A line graph shows how something changes over time; the horizontal axis is usually time
Rising lines mean increasing, falling lines mean decreasing, flat lines mean no change
Steepness shows how fast it changes, not how big the value is
Joining points makes sense only when the quantity exists between the points (height, temperature), not for separate categories (favourite fruits)
A scale that doesn't start at zero, or is uneven, can make changes look bigger than they are

misconceptions.belief: Joins points for category data where the in-between values mean nothing
signs: Draws a line graph of favourite fruits
Reads a value 'between mango and banana'
Uses line graphs for any table

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which data suits a line graph?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa data line graph ke liye theek hai?

options.text: Temperature every hour through a day
Number of students who like each fruit
Number of boys and girls in a class

remediation.representation: Both data sets drawn as line graphs, with the in-between point marked and questioned
remediation.moveShape: Child tries to say what the midpoint of each line means; ask which midpoint describes something real

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the steepest part of a line graph is where the value is highest
signs: Says AQI was highest where the line rose fastest
Confuses rate of change with value
Reads slope instead of height

diagnostic.prompt_en: On a line graph, the steepest climb is from Nov 1 to Nov 5, but the highest point is on Nov 10. When was the value highest?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Line graph mein sabse tez chadhai Nov 1 se Nov 5 tak hai, par sabse ooncha point Nov 10 pe hai. Value sabse zyada kab thi?

options.text: Between Nov 1 and Nov 5, where it is steepest

remediation.representation: A graph with a ruler slid along the vertical axis to read heights, versus a slope triangle drawn on each segment
remediation.moveShape: Child reads the height at each point, then compares slopes; ask which question each tool answers

misconceptions.belief: Reads a graph without checking whether the axis starts at zero, so small changes look huge
signs: Says a change from 120 to 124 'more than doubled' from the picture
Ignores the numbers on the axis
Compares bar or line heights instead of values

diagnostic.prompt_en: A graph's vertical axis starts at 120 cm. A child's height goes from 121 cm to 125 cm and the line looks very steep. Did the height grow a lot?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek graph ka vertical axis 120 cm se shuru hota hai. Bachche ki height 121 cm se 125 cm hoti hai aur line bahut tez chadhti dikhti hai. Kya height bahut badhi?

options.text: Only 4 cm; the axis starting at 120 makes it look bigger
Yes, because the line is steep

remediation.representation: The same data redrawn with the axis starting at 0
remediation.moveShape: Child compares the two drawings; ask which one shows the change honestly and why

items.prompt_en: A line graph shows a child's height: age 8: 125 cm, 9: 129 cm, 10: 136 cm, 11: 141 cm. How much did the child grow from age 10 to 11?
items.prompt_hi: Ek line graph bachche ki height dikhata hai: 8 saal: 125 cm, 9: 129 cm, 10: 136 cm, 11: 141 cm. 10 se 11 saal mein kitna badha?
items.answer: 5 cm

items.prompt_en: Using the same graph, between which two ages did the child grow the most?
items.prompt_hi: Usi graph se batao, kin do umron ke beech bachcha sabse zyada badha?
items.answer: Between 9 and 10 (7 cm)

items.prompt_en: From the same graph, estimate the child's height at 9½ years.
items.prompt_hi: Usi graph se andaaza lagao: 9½ saal pe bachche ki height kitni thi?
items.answer: About 132-133 cm (halfway between 129 and 136)

items.prompt_en: Which of these should be shown as a line graph: (a) temperature every hour in a day; (b) favourite fruits of a class (mango 12, banana 8, apple 5)? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Inmein se kise line graph se dikhana chahiye: (a) din bhar har ghante ka taapmaan; (b) class ke pasandida phal (aam 12, kela 8, seb 5)? Kyun?
items.answer: (a): temperature exists between the hours, so joining points makes sense; (b) is separate categories, better as a bar graph
hints: What would a point halfway between two hours mean?
The temperature at half past: real.
What would a point halfway between mango and banana mean?

items.prompt_en: Kiran drew a line graph joining 'mango 12', 'banana 8' and 'apple 5'. What is wrong with joining these points?
items.prompt_hi: Kiran ne 'aam 12', 'kela 8' aur 'seb 5' ko jodte hue line graph banaya. In points ko jodne mein kya galat hai?
items.answer: Fruits are separate categories; there's nothing 'between' mango and banana, so the line means nothing. Use a bar graph
hints: What does the line between mango and banana stand for?
Nothing: there is no fruit halfway.
Bar graph, not a line graph.

items.prompt_en: Why is it fine to join the points on a graph of a plant's height measured each week?
items.prompt_hi: Har hafte naapi gayi paudhe ki height ke graph mein points ko jodna kyun theek hai?
items.answer: The plant had a height at every moment between measurements, and it changed smoothly, so the line gives sensible in-between estimates
hints: Did the plant have a height on days you didn't measure?
Yes, it was growing all the time.
So points between the dots show ___ values.
The line estimates real in-between heights.

items.prompt_en: Delhi AQI readings: Nov 1: 180, Nov 5: 320, Nov 10: 410, Nov 15: 290. On which date was the AQI highest, and how much did it fall from then to Nov 15?
items.prompt_hi: Delhi AQI readings: Nov 1: 180, Nov 5: 320, Nov 10: 410, Nov 15: 290. AQI kis din sabse zyada tha, aur us din se Nov 15 tak kitna gira?
items.answer: Highest on Nov 10 (410); it fell by 120 to 290

items.prompt_en: On the AQI graph, Riya says: 'The line from Nov 1 to Nov 5 is the steepest, so the AQI was highest then.' Correct her.
items.prompt_hi: AQI graph pe Riya kehti hai: 'Nov 1 se Nov 5 ki line sabse tez chadhti hai, toh tab AQI sabse zyada tha.' Use theek karo.
items.answer: Steepest means it rose fastest (by 140) then; the highest value was 410 on Nov 10
hints: Does a steep line tell you how high, or how fast?
The highest point on the graph is on ___
Fastest rise Nov 1-5; highest value Nov 10.

items.prompt_en: You want to plot AQI values from 0 to 450 on graph paper with 10 cm of height. What scale would you choose?
items.prompt_hi: Tum 0 se 450 tak ke AQI values graph paper pe plot karna chahte ho jismein 10 cm oonchai hai. Kaunsa scale chunoge?
items.answer: 1 cm = 50 units (450 needs 9 cm)
hints: What is the largest value to fit?

items.prompt_en: A line graph shows a train's distance from the station over time. Between 10:20 and 10:35 the line is flat. What was the train doing?
items.prompt_hi: Ek line graph train ki station se doori samay ke saath dikhata hai. 10:20 se 10:35 tak line flat hai. Train kya kar rahi thi?
items.answer: It was stopped: its distance didn't change for 15 minutes
hints: What does a flat line mean about the quantity?
If distance doesn't change, the train is ___

items.prompt_en: A graph of a child's height uses a vertical axis starting at 120 cm. The line from 121 cm to 125 cm looks huge. What's misleading, and what's the real change?
items.prompt_hi: Ek bachche ki height ke graph ka vertical axis 120 cm se shuru hota hai. 121 cm se 125 cm ki line bahut badi dikhti hai. Kya gumraah karne wala hai, aur asli badlaav kitna hai?
items.answer: The axis doesn't start at 0, which stretches small changes; the real change is only 4 cm
hints: Where does the vertical axis start?
Only 4 cm; the cut axis exaggerates it.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how to read a line graph: what rising, falling, flat and steep parts mean.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki line graph kaise padhte hain: chadhti, girti, flat aur tez hisson ka kya matlab hai.
items.answer: Rising means increasing, falling means decreasing, flat means no change; steeper means faster change; read values from the height of a point on the vertical axis
acceptable: rising increases, flat no change, steep fast
hints: What does the height of a point tell you?
And what does the steepness of a segment tell you?
Up = increase, down = decrease, flat = none, steep = fast.

items.prompt_en: On a line graph, what does a line going down from left to right mean?
items.prompt_hi: Line graph pe baayein se daayein neeche jaati line ka kya matlab hai?
items.answer: The quantity is decreasing over time
hints: What is on the horizontal axis?
Time, moving forward to the right.
As time goes on, the value goes ___

workedExample.problem: Temperatures were 6 am: 18 °C, 9 am: 24 °C, 12 pm: 31 °C, 3 pm: 33 °C, 6 pm: 27 °C. Describe the trend and find the fastest rise.
steps: Plot time on the horizontal axis and temperature on the vertical axis.
The line rises from 6 am to 3 pm, then falls to 6 pm.
The fastest rise is 9 am to 12 pm (+7 °C), the steepest part.
The highest temperature is 33 °C at 3 pm.
fadedVersion: Plot ___ on the horizontal axis and temperature on the vertical axis.
The line rises from 6 am to ___, then falls to 6 pm.
The fastest rise is 9 am to 12 pm, the ___ part.
The highest temperature is ___ at 3 pm.

skills.title: Write the steps of a think-of-a-number trick as an algebraic expression
Simplify the expression to explain why the trick always works

items.prompt_hi: Trapezium ke formula mein ½ × (a + b) × h kyun hota hai?
items.answer: Two identical trapeziums, one turned upside down, fit into a parallelogram with base a + b and height h; one trapezium is half of that
hints: Put two copies together, one flipped. What shape forms?
Its base is a + b and its area is ___
Half of (a + b) × h for one trapezium.

items.prompt_en: An L-shaped room can be split into two rectangles in two different ways. Predict: will both ways give the same area?
items.prompt_hi: Ek L-shape ke kamre ko do alag tareekon se do rectangles mein baanta ja sakta hai. Guess karo: kya dono tareekon se same area aayega?
items.answer: Yes; the floor is the same, however you split it
hints: Does cutting a shape change how much floor there is?
No, cutting only regroups the floor.

items.prompt_en: An L-shaped room is a 10 m by 8 m rectangle with a 4 m by 3 m corner cut out. Find its area.
items.prompt_hi: Ek L-shape ka kamra 10 m by 8 m ka rectangle hai jiske corner se 4 m by 3 m kaat diya gaya. Area nikaalo.
items.answer: 68 m²

items.prompt_en: For the same L-shaped room (10 m by 8 m with a 4 m by 3 m corner removed from the top right), find the area by splitting into a 10 m by 5 m rectangle and a 6 m by 3 m rectangle. Compare with subtracting.
items.prompt_hi: Usi L-shape kamre (10 m by 8 m, top right se 4 m by 3 m corner hataaya) ka area 10 m by 5 m aur 6 m by 3 m rectangles mein baant ke nikaalo. Ghataane wale tareeke se compare karo.
items.answer: 50 + 18 = 68 m², the same as 80 − 12

items.prompt_en: The front wall of a hut is a 6 m wide, 4 m tall rectangle with a triangular gable on top (base 6 m, height 2 m). Find the wall's total area.
items.prompt_hi: Ek jhopdi ki saamne ki deewar 6 m chaudi, 4 m oonchi rectangle hai jiske upar triangle wala hissa hai (base 6 m, height 2 m). Deewar ka kul area nikaalo.
hints: Split into a rectangle and a triangle.

items.prompt_en: A 2 m wide path runs all around the outside of a 20 m by 10 m garden. Find the area of the path.
items.prompt_hi: 20 m by 10 m ke garden ke chaaron taraf bahar 2 m chauda raasta hai. Raaste ka area nikaalo.
items.answer: 136 m²
hints: What are the outer dimensions with the path?

items.prompt_en: A trapezium has parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm and height 4 cm. Find its area by thinking of it as a rectangle whose width is the average of the parallel sides.
items.prompt_hi: Ek trapezium ki parallel sides 6 cm aur 10 cm aur height 4 cm hai. Ise aisa rectangle maan ke area nikaalo jiski chaudai parallel sides ka average ho.
items.answer: Average width 8 cm, so area = 8 × 4 = 32 cm²
hints: What is the average of 6 and 10?

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend two ways to find the area of an L-shape, and why both must give the same answer.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko L-shape ka area nikaalne ke do tareeke samjhao, aur batao dono ka answer same kyun aana chahiye.
items.answer: Either split it into two rectangles and add, or take a big rectangle and subtract the missing corner; both measure the same floor, so they must agree (and don't count any overlap twice)
acceptable: split and add, or subtract the cut-out
hints: What is one way to cut the L?
Add parts or subtract the gap; the floor is the same, so the totals agree.

items.prompt_en: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm and height 4 cm.
items.prompt_hi: 5 cm aur 9 cm parallel sides aur 4 cm height wale trapezium ka area nikaalo.
items.answer: 28 cm²
